title: Kenny Pickett introductory press conference | Carolina Panthers
text: Hey Kenny, how's it going, man? Thanks for taking the time to do this. Yeah, absolutely, man. Um firstly, can you just explain what made coming to Carolina an attractive thing for you while you were in free agency? Yeah, I think number one, I think coach Canales and the track record he has with with quarterbacks and and all the places he's been and you know, over the over his career, I've watched a lot of tape. I've seen him at different places. Really like what he really like what he does. I feel like it's been similar to what I've done in college and what I did in Philly. So start off the bat, I think that that was number one for me. What specifically do you know about Dave Canales and his history with quarterbacks? Yeah, so I was just with Geno Smith over in Vegas and Geno had nothing but great things to say about him. So that was great, you know, to to hear it from a player that you know, worked with him. You know, it was awesome. He was at my pro day actually four years ago. I grabbed lunch with him at at Fat Heads down in South Side in Pittsburgh and really just enjoyed my time with him, you know, just a great person. One of the guys that you really want to be around in this in this league in this profession. It's a tough business, but you know, great people make it a lot easier. Yeah, so you know, just from a track record standpoint, that's kind of as far as we go back and then having Geno to kind of ask questions to is great. And final thing about Dave cuz those are interesting answers. Have you watched how he's kind of brought this Carolina offense to life over the past couple years as well? Yeah, I have. You know, my time in Philly they played us, you know, right down to the wire, you know, you know, in Philly and you know, really like the things they were doing. Similar to what I felt like what we were doing you know, with Kellen Moore and and what we were doing in Philly. So I thought it would be, you know, a really good fit for me to play here. Awesome, thanks. You got it. David Newton followed by Jeff Hawkins. Hey Kenny, David Newton with the espn.com. So with Canales he's got like you said the reputation for really developing quarterbacks. Um have you given up at all on being a starter? I mean, kind of where are you on that right now? Is that just you feel What do you feel like needs to be developed to get you back to that level, I guess is the question. Yeah, I just really wanted to get in a great system with with great people. I think that's just where I'm at right now. Taking it a day at a time, working really hard this off season. You know, just to improve my game in the weight room, on the field. Now that I finally, you know, got a playbook and can watch some tape and kind of dive into this this new system is is really my main concern now. So I'm really not trying to look, you know, too far down the road. I want to be a positive addition to this team and help any way I can. And what are your as far as Bryce goes, what's your relationship with him? Have y'all had one? I mean, you know, you're only a class or two apart in in the draft. So kind of tell me about that and what's your impression of his journey so far and some of the struggles he's had and anything you can relate to. Yeah, Bryce is a great guy. We go back to the Heisman in 2021 was the first time I met him. You know, we had a joint practice against Carolina when I was when I was in Cleveland. I was hurt so I really didn't get to do too much, but I was able to, you know, talk to him kind of there you know, at the practice and and before the game. You know, he's a great guy. Respect him and his journey that he's been on. You know, seems like he's constantly working, constantly trying to improve and seems like a great person. So definitely looking forward to working with him. Thank you very much. Appreciate it. Thank you. Good afternoon and good luck this year. Thank you. Along with the your relationship with Bryce, do you have any type of a history with any of the anyone in the in the receiver room or tight end room? Um off the top of my head now, not in the receiver. Actually, you know what? I Smith, I believe is is here. You know, I was with him in Philly and and we got to work together a lot. Great guy, you know, really rooting for him. It'll be awesome to see him in the locker room again. He's got a great personality. So excited to work with him. I was teammates actually with Pat Jones who's on the defensive side at the University of Pittsburgh for four years and we you know, we developed a really good friendship and I know he's a big fisherman. So that's something I hope we can we can do in the spring together. You're a fisherman, too? I am, yeah, a little bit. Well, you have a few opportunities around here. Perfect. what is your reflections on the bowl game that you played at Bank of America Stadium and the play that resulted in the in the rule change? Do you reflect on that at all or or what What is the your smile there? What was that game like? It's a great memory. That's why I'm smiling. You know, that that was a special night you know, to do it in in Charlotte in the ACC championship game and you know, guys I played with for for five years. I was a five-year guy and it's all we talked about was winning the ACC championship. So the fact that's my home stadium now, I think it's pretty cool and you know, hopefully we can make some more great memories this season. And that play? Yeah, it was all just kind of, you know, improv, I guess. Just just playing playing football. They pulled up so far away. I was going to go down and slide and figured I'm not supposed to keep going. So it worked out well. Hey, good luck this year. Joe Person. Kenny, congrats. Welcome to Charlotte. Thank you. I am wondering and David asked you this variation of this question, but when you see guys like Daniel Jones and and Malik Willis, you know, kind of a a second chapter in their career, so to speak, as starters. Is that something and I know you said that's not first and foremost with you here, but is that something, you know, you that you kind of look forward to and hope you get a shot to to write your own second chapter? Yeah, of course. That's that's you know, the the ultimate the ultimate goal. But I think it's just, you know, things happen in this league. You just keep working cuz you never know when that opportunity is going to come. You know, I just want to be as prepared as I can be. You never know when that's going to happen. I just want to put my best foot forward. Wanted to ask you, too. I'm I'm old enough to remember Matt Rhule and Scott Fitterer, you know, coming to your pro day and really, you know, evaluating you pretty, you know, pretty seriously. What what What do you remember about that pre-draft where the Panthers were concerned specifically? Yeah, it was obviously a whole new um staff and building and a lot of new faces this time around, you know, coming down here. You know, but yeah, that whole draft process is crazy. The the pro day, everyone was there and I had a, you know, pre-draft um visit down in Charlotte. Got to see the city a little bit more. So from that standpoint, that's about it. That that was kind of the same. You know, I'm excited now that I'm here. I can, you know, get around the city a little bit more and you know, get to know everybody in the building. Thanks, Kenny. You got it. Alex Zietlow. Kenny, we asked you about Bryce, but do you do you know Andy Dalton at all in a professional capacity? Do you remember growing up watching him? What's your I guess, like how do you know Andy? Yeah, I I grew up watching him, obviously, you know, just like a lot of young quarterbacks coming up. Um And then usually but before every game that I've just about played Andy, you know, we kind of catch up for 10 to 15 minutes just being in the, you know, the quarterback uh I guess like fraternity here in the league that you just, you know, talk to guys before the game. You know, he's he's an awesome guy from all of my experiences. So I'm definitely excited to, you know, be in the room with him and and learn as much as I can from him. And you'll you've been in uh offseason situations, training camp situations where there've been quarterback battles. Uh how do you go about approaching that sort of thing, particularly with players that you've grown up admiring and stuff like this? Yeah, I think it's more of a a media fan spectacle than it is a a player deal. You know, regardless if you're in a competition or not, you're showing up to compete. You know, nothing really changes at least from my my my point of view. Like I'm going in there every day to be the best player I can be to try to improve. So that's the same if there is a competition or if there isn't. You know, so I don't think my life changes too much. Got it. Thanks. You got it, man. Thank you. Any more questions for Kenny? All right, Kenny. Thanks so much for taking the time to talk to us. Yeah, appreciate you guys. >> [music] [music]

Um, and just taking it to the football field. And I love the I love the game of football, so it's it's easy for me to play hard. It's easy for me to um just play with passion because I love it. >> Awesome. Thanks. Welcome to Detroit. Thank you, Will. >> Hey, Greg. I guess just tell us a little more about your story, uh, coming out of high school. Then it looks like you've got tons of experience as a return man in the NFL. Kick returns, punt returns. Last year seemed to be maybe your most efficient as a return man on punts, a careerhigh in yards per return.
